newsitem.title: USA: DEERE FINANCIAL SERVICES UNITS Q3 NET DOWN. [CORRECTED 21:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: DEERE FINANCIAL SERVICES UNITS Q3 NET DOWN. [CORRECTED 21:34 GMT]

text.p: Deere & Co said Tuesday net income generated by its financial services subsidiaries fell during the third quarter ended July 31 to $26.8 million from $48.1 million during the same period in 1996.
Year-to-date net income for the financial services group was $110.2 million, off from $149.2 million during the same year-ago period, the company said in an earnings statement.
Health care operations lost $21.4 million net for the quarter and $19.6 million year-to-date versus net income of $4.8 million and $13.2 million, respectively, last year.
It tied health care losses to continued higher claims costs, reduced margins due to high competition, strengthening of health care claims reserves, and higher costs.
Charges from the planned closure at year-end of two of seven John Deere Medical Group health care centers in Des Moines were recorded in the quarter, it said.
A company spokeswoman said charges from those closings would represent a "relatively small portion of losses in the area, but we have not quantified the costs."
The two centers provide health care for about 1,100 Deere employees and families and 800 non-Deere customers under a professional contract and do not use Deere employees as staff.

Deere has five health centers still open and 20 health operations that provide services to 1,400 (corrects number of health centres and type of operation) companies nationwide covering about 410,000 people.

Net third-quarter income of the credit operations was $41.6 million, up from $35.3 million a year earlier. For the first nine months 1997, income stood at $106.1 million, off from $109.7 million in the same nine months in 1996.

It said third-quarter earnings in credit operations reflect higher income from a larger average receivable and lease portfolio and gains from sale of retail notes. It tied lower year-to-date results to narrower financing spreads and higher costs from several growth efforts, which were partly offset by higher income from the larger average portfolio.
Insurance operations produced net quarterly income of $6.6 million and $23.7 million year-to-date versus $8.0 million and $26.3 million, respectively, in the comparable 1996 periods.
Deere & Co reported third-quarter earnings Tuesday of $1.00 per share versus $0.79 in the year-ago period.
